title: Jensen Huang on AI factories: the five-layer cake and why AI elevates jobs
summary: Jensen explains AI from first principles: computing shifted from retrieval to real-time generation, so the world needs vast AI factories producing tokens, like the dynamo and the internet before. He gives a five-layer model for investing and argues task versus purpose shows AI elevates jobs.

principles.text: Go back to first principles: computing shifted from retrieving pre-recorded files to generating intelligence in real time.
principles.quote: Went from a computer industry that was largely based on retrieval for 60 years, and all of a sudden, one day, it's completely generated in real time. We call it intelligence.

principles.text: Reason upstream (industrially) about a new capability, not only about downstream industries, to position in large markets.
principles.quote: But you should go upstream, meaning industrially, what does that mean? And so, the first thing you realize is this. Go back to first principles.

principles.text: Think of AI as a five-layer cake (energy, chips, infrastructure, models, applications) to decide where to invest.
principles.quote: And so, this five-layer cake is the industrial version. And I think that's a good way to think about where to invest.

principles.text: AI can learn anything with predictable structure, so the opportunity reaches far beyond language models into the physical world.
principles.quote: we hear we talk about all the language, but don't forget we learn any you can learn anything with structure.

principles.text: Separate task from purpose: automating tasks doesn't remove the job, it elevates it.
principles.quote: Typing is not the job of a software engineer. Coding is not their job. Solving problems is their job.

principles.text: Don't fear AI, engage it. You lose out to people who use AI, not to AI itself.
principles.quote: You may or may not lose a job to an AI. But you will absolutely lose a job to someone who uses AI.
